speaker: gauge
text: Old skyscrapers look like wedding cakes. Build straight up. More room.

speaker: fitz
text: Wait. The Equitable Building did that in 1915. Its shadow fell across its neighbors.

speaker: fitz
text:
That was the worry. In 1916, New York passed the country's first comprehensive zoning law.
Above a certain height, towers had to step back inside a slanted line, so light and air could reach the street.
A slim tower could rise without limit over a quarter of the lot.

speaker: gauge
text: Ooh, what else is built weird? Subscribe and let's find out.
